title: How Starbucks spilled coffee on its digital strategy with loyalty changes

facts.fact: According to the article, the Starbucks loyalty program changes ended the coffee giant's streak of 25 straight quarters of growth.
facts.quote: the end result has been an end to the coffee giant’s 25 straight quarters of growth.

facts.fact: Starbucks Rewards changed from a frequency-based model to a spend-based model, under which free drinks are earned based on how much money customers spend over time.
facts.quote: the strategic shift of our tremendously successful loyalty program from a frequency-based to a spend-based model

facts.fact: According to Starbucks CEO Howard Schultz, the loyalty program shift was a one-time event that he described as a once-in-a-decade change.
facts.quote: The shift was a one-time event, a once-in-a-decade change built on carefully vetted analysis

facts.fact: Starbucks stated that the spend-based model would instantly eliminate order splitting, a practice in which customers split up orders to earn rewards points more quickly.
facts.quote: the shift would instantly eliminate a vexing in-store operating issue, order splitting

facts.fact: Starbucks' Frappuccino Happy Hour is described as an annual nationwide promotion that typically ushers in the busiest time of year in its stores.
facts.quote: our annual Frappuccino Happy Hour promotion, a nationwide event that typically ushers in the busiest time of year in our stores

facts.fact: Schultz acknowledged that Starbucks did not execute as well as it could have in the US in Q3 in certain areas.
facts.quote: in certain areas, we did not execute as well as we could have in the US in Q3.
